# Implementation Plan: Hard-crash member-crashed auto-notify v1 (crews)
<!-- ralph-meta {"overviewTaskId":"crews-member-crash-auto-notify-lead"} -->

*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph` on 2026-06-07. Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan D:/harness-efforts/codexu/.ralph/jobs/crews-member-crash-auto-notify-lead/plan.md`.*
*Seeded from brainstorm: `.ralph/brainstorms/crews-member-crash-auto-notify-lead/selected-direction.md` (D-001 + D-003, hard-crash-only v1).*

## Overview

When a crew **member** dies a **high-confidence hard death** (`getMemberHealth` → `state:'dead'`:
launcher pid gone, or no-pid + heartbeat stale past `HEARTBEAT_STALE_MS`), the crew **lead** is
pushed **exactly one** `review-required` `member-crashed` notification through the existing
mailbox/armed-listener channel — **including when the lead is idle on an indefinitely-armed
listener** (the failure mode that motivated the task: the 2026-06-06 silent brainstorm-member
deaths and the ~9h-dark incident). No new lead-model poll loop; the lead never has to manually
`/crews-list-members` to discover a dead member.

The load-bearing mechanism (**D-001**) piggybacks a **throttled (≤1/60s) liveness sweep** on the
lead listener's existing heartbeat `setInterval` (`lib/listener-loop.js:305-353`) — the only
periodic hook that fires during a quiet, indefinitely-armed (`timeoutMs===null`) idle wait. A
**turn-boundary backstop (D-003)** runs the same sweep at the lead's Stop/PreToolUse/SessionStart
boundaries for the actively-working lead and owns latch-reset hygiene. Dedupe is **generation-scoped**
(signature per member incarnation), so a resumed-then-re-crashed member notifies again and repeated
sweeps over the same corpse never duplicate.

This is a **crews submodule** change (`ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/`); it follows the
two-commit submodule flow and the standard 6-file version bump + CHANGELOG. **Stalled/idle (9h-dark)
detection is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE** (separate task `crews-member-stalled-needs-attention-nudge`).

## Research Findings

### Codebase Context
crews is JavaScript/CommonJS, no package.json; tests via `node tests/run.js` (worker-per-file,
concurrency 10, <60s target), "typecheck" = `node --check <file>`. Strict schema CI:
`CREWS_STRICT_SCHEMA=1`.

Key seams (all verified file:line):
- **`lib/listener-loop.js:305-353`** — heartbeat `setInterval(..., HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS)`; the ONLY
  periodic code path during an idle indefinite listener. Closure var `consecutiveHeartbeatFailures`
  (`:304`) is the precedent for a `lastCrashSweepAt` throttle var. `deliver(reason)` (`:356-393`)
  calls `consumeMailbox(...)` then `finish({type:'messages', count, ..., via:reason})`; it is a
  hoisted function declaration callable from the heartbeat callback. `timeoutMs===null` ⇒ no
  timeout/poll timers install except the heartbeat + the fs.watch + the poll backstop.
- **`hooks/health.js`** — `getMemberHealth(name, crew, stateCwd)` (`:66-96`) returns
  `{name, crew, state, launcherPid, launcherStartedAt, pidAlive, lastHeartbeatAt, lastTurnAt,
  queuedMailboxCount, unreviewedReviewRequired, actorState, listenerState, reason}`. **Does NOT
  return `sessionId` or `createdBy`** (both read from the manifest internally). `deriveHealthState`
  (`:46-64`): `dead` iff `pidAlive===false` OR (`pidAlive===null && heartbeatAge>=HEARTBEAT_STALE_MS`);
  `quiet`/`unknown`/`alive`/`cleared`/`left` otherwise. `isProcessAlive` (`:13-23`) treats EPERM as
  alive (documented false negative). Constants in `hooks/actors.js:114-118`:
  `HEARTBEAT_ALIVE_MS=30_000`, `HEARTBEAT_STALE_MS=5*60_000`.
- **`hooks/mailbox.js`** — `appendSystemMailbox(name, crew, cwd, messageOrEnvelope, opts)` (`:541-582`)
  stamps `from.role='system'`, `from.routingKind = opts.kind || 'thread-fanout'`, validates via
  `buildEnvelope` (strict throws), routes through `appendMailboxWithSender` (`:438-494`). This is the
  delivery seam used by `member-left`/`member-joined`/`member-reply`/`proactive-report`.
- **`hooks/protocol/envelope.js`** — `kindEnum` `:63-88` (18 kinds); `PAYLOAD_RULES` `:96-137`.
- **`hooks/protocol/review-required.js`** — `DEFAULT_REVIEW_KINDS` `:1-12`. `envelopeKind` falls back
  to `from.routingKind` when `env.kind` absent.
- **`hooks/stop.js`** — `ACK_EXEMPT_KINDS` `:189-196`; exemption test `:264`
  (`from.role==='system' && ACK_EXEMPT_KINDS.has(from.routingKind)`).
- **`hooks/actors.js:1144-1153`** — `listNames(crew, cwd)` enumerates members+leads+tasks roots.
- **`hooks/commands/resume-crew.js:276-360`** — `repairManifestForResume`; rewrites
  `listenerState:'recoverable'`, `lastListenerPid:null` (`:333-339`).
- **`hooks/commands/clear-member.js:63-87`** — clear-member handler.
- **`tests/protocol-manifest.test.js:22`** — `equal(manifestFields.length, 51, ...)`. A new top-level
  manifest field bumps this to 52.

### Technical Constraints
- The listener stdout `{type:'messages', count, name, crew, sessionId, via}` envelope is intentionally
  stable; new diagnostics belong in `crews.log`, not stdout.
- The heartbeat write path already has EPERM/UNKNOWN auto-recovery; the sweep must NOT add
  high-frequency manifest writes or lock pressure — hence the ≤1/60s throttle.
- Manifest schema has an exact-count test (`manifestFields.length===51`). A **separate crew-level latch
  file** avoids BOTH the count churn AND the member-manifest write-race with `repairManifestForResume`,
  and is multi-lead clean. (Chosen over `manifest.custom.*`.)
- Health detection deliberately fails toward false negatives. Do NOT reinterpret `quiet`/`unknown`/
  EPERM-as-alive as a crash.
- Mailbox and manifest locks are separate domains; the latch needs its own explicit lock + atomic write.

## Approach

### Architecture

A new focused helper module **`hooks/member-crash-notifications.js`** owns all scan/dedupe/latch logic
(keeps it out of the listener-loop and the three hook entrypoints, and makes it unit-testable). Exports:

- `buildDeadSignature(health)` → canonical string of `{memberName, sessionId, launcherPid,
  launcherStartedAt, takeoverAt, deadReason}`. **`takeoverAt` is load-bearing** (see F-002 below):
  same-session `/resume-crew` reuses `sessionId`, and `launcher.pid` is rewritten only when the new
  launcher script runs at runtime (`actors.js:2435-2436`), NOT by `repairManifestForResume` — so
  without `takeoverAt` a re-crash before the new launcher.pid is written would carry the OLD corpse's
  signature and be suppressed. `takeoverAt` is stamped on every resume/takeover
  (`writeMemberTakeoverManifest` `actors.js:522,533`), so it reliably changes the signature per
  incarnation.
- `sweepMemberCrashNotifications({ leadName, crew, cwd, now })` → enumerates member actors, applies the
  skip guards (below), detects high-confidence-dead transitions vs the latch, appends ONE
  `member-crashed` envelope per new dead incarnation to the **lead's own mailbox**, persists the latch
  after each successful append, and returns `{ appended: <count>, notified: [names] }` so the caller
  (listener) can decide whether to self-deliver.
- `resetMemberCrashNotificationLatch({ leadName, crew, cwd, memberName })` → clears one member's latch
  entry (used by resume + clear-member). A `leadName`-less variant clears the member across all leads.
- Internal locked latch read/write over `<crewRoot>/liveness-notifications.json`.

**Latch persist-after-append ordering (F-006):** persist the latch entry ONLY after the
`appendSystemMailbox` succeeds. If the append succeeds but the subsequent latch write fails (EPERM/etc.),
the design is intentionally **fail-loud / fail-duplicate**: the next sweep MAY re-notify the same
incarnation. Log a `member-crash-latch-write-failed name=<member> crew=<crew>` crews.log line and
accept the rare duplicate over a dropped notification. Add a unit test covering append-ok-but-latch-write-fail.

**Latch file** `<crewRoot>/liveness-notifications.json`, shape:
```json
{ "memberCrash": { "<leadName>": { "<memberName>": "<signature>" } } }
```
Keyed by `leadName` first so each lead has its own dedupe namespace (multi-lead clean; matches the
delivery model — the sweep appends to the CURRENT lead's own mailbox). Guarded by a dedicated lock
(`withStateFileLock`/`withManifestLock`-style) and `writeJsonAtomic`/`writeJsonAtomicWithRetry`
(EPERM/UNKNOWN-tolerant per v3.5.0/v3.8.0).

**Generation-scoped dedupe + explicit reset are BOTH load-bearing (corrected per F-002).** The
signature (now including `takeoverAt`) is the primary dedupe: a resumed member has a fresh `takeoverAt`
→ a fresh signature → it re-notifies on a subsequent crash. The explicit reset on resume + clear-member
is **REQUIRED, not just hygiene** — it (a) GCs stale entries for members that crash and are never
resumed, and (b) covers the failed-spawn / no-new-launcher.pid window. Reset semantics: clear the
member's latch entry in `repairManifestForResume`; if the respawn then fails the member stays dead and
SHOULD re-notify (correct), and the fresh `takeoverAt` guarantees the re-notification is a single fresh
row, not a duplicate of the old signature.

### Sweep skip guards (the heart of "high-confidence, not a false alarm")

For each enumerated actor the sweep MUST skip unless ALL hold; notify ONLY on a genuine unexpected
hard death:
1. **Member role only** — skip the sweeping lead itself, other leads, and task actors
   (`manifest.role !== 'member'`).
2. **Not intentionally stopped** — skip if `manifest.shutdownRequested === true` OR
   `manifest.terminationKind` is set OR `manifest.terminatedAt` is set. *(A `/stop-member` hard-kill
   leaves `pidAlive===false` → `state:'dead'`; without this guard every intentional stop would
   false-fire a crash alert. Load-bearing.)* **CORRECTED per F-001 — the guard alone is INSUFFICIENT:**
   `applyHardStopMember` (`hooks/actors.js:1529`) kills the process (`hardTerminateMemberByLauncherChildren`
   at `:1548`) BEFORE writing the shutdown markers (`:1601-1611`). A sweep landing in that kill→markers
   window sees a dead pid with no markers → false alert. **Fix (in scope): hoist a pre-kill
   `shutdownRequested:true` (intent) manifest write into `applyHardStopMember` BEFORE the kill** (the
   soft path already writes shutdownRequested first at `:1451-1457`; mirror it), leaving the
   `terminationKind`/`terminatedAt`/`terminatedPids` audit write after the kill. Add a regression test
   that forces a sweep between the (stubbed) kill and the final audit write.
3. **Not mid-resume** — skip if `manifest.listenerState === 'recoverable'` (a member being resumed has
   its old launcher pid killed, so it transiently reads `dead`).
4. **Not already terminal-state** — `deriveHealthState` already returns `cleared`/`left` (not `dead`)
   for those actorStates, so `state==='dead'` covers this, but assert it.
5. **Owned by this lead** — normalize ownership via the EXISTING `createdByLeadName(manifest.createdBy)`
   helper (`hooks/stop.js:392` / `hooks/actors.js:1376`; handles both string and `{leadName}` object
   forms) — NOT a raw `createdBy.leadName` read (F-004). When `createdByLeadName` resolves to this lead,
   claim it. When it is null: claim ONLY if this is the sole ACTIVE lead, determined via
   `activeLeadNames(meta, crew, cwd)` (`hooks/actors.js:849`) — NOT raw `readCrewMeta().leads` (which can
   include tombstoned/inactive leads). When null `createdBy` is NOT claimable (multi-active-lead crew),
   emit a `member-crash-sweep-orphan-skipped name=<member> crew=<crew>` crews.log line so the silent
   miss is discoverable. *(Note: `assignMemberRole` seeds member manifests WITHOUT `createdBy`
   (`actors.js:719-728`); only `/spawn-member` sets `{leadName}` (`spawn-member.js:169-193`) — so
   null-createdBy members are a real population, not a corner case.)*
6. **High-confidence dead** — `health.state === 'dead'` (NEVER `quiet`/`unknown`/`alive`).

### Detection plumbing
The sweep needs `sessionId` (for the signature) and `createdBy` + `role` + the intentional-shutdown
markers (for the guards). `getMemberHealth` already reads the manifest but does not return these.
**Extend `getMemberHealth`'s return object** (additive: `sessionId`, `createdBy`, `role`, `takeoverAt`,
`shutdownRequested`, `terminationKind`, `terminatedAt`) — this is a return-shape change, NOT a
`manifestFields` change, so the `manifestFields.length===51` test is untouched. **The extension MUST be
strictly additive (F-005):** `snapshotCrew()` calls `getMemberHealth` for EVERY `listNames` entry
(leads + tasks too), so do NOT make `getMemberHealth` member-role-strict or change any existing return
field, or `/crews-list-members` / status surfaces regress. Add a `health.test.js` assertion that the
new fields are present and the existing shape is unchanged. (Alternatively the sweep re-reads the
manifest; the extend-return path is preferred for single-source + less IO, but either satisfies the
ACs.)

### D-001 — heartbeat-tick liveness monitor (load-bearing core)
In `lib/listener-loop.js`, inside the heartbeat `setInterval` callback (`:305-353`), AFTER the
`markArmed` heartbeat write + `decideHeartbeatAction` handling and ONLY when the actor is a lead:
- Throttle: a module-local closure var `lastCrashSweepAt` (init 0); run the sweep only when
  `now - lastCrashSweepAt >= CRASH_SWEEP_THROTTLE_MS` (default 60_000, env override
  `CREWS_CRASH_SWEEP_THROTTLE_MS`). Set `lastCrashSweepAt = now` before the sweep.
- Wrap the whole sweep in try/catch (observability/best-effort — a sweep error must NEVER crash the
  heartbeat timer or the listener; log `member-crash-sweep-failed ... err=...` to crews.log and continue).
- If `sweep.appended > 0`, call the existing `deliver('crash-sweep')` **synchronously in the same tick**
  so the just-appended envelope is consumed in the same wake (append-before-consume; avoids the
  v3.12.0 delayed-delivery shape). `deliver` already guards `count===0` (no spurious exit). The stdout
  envelope shape is unchanged (`via='crash-sweep'` is a new `via` value, consistent with the existing
  `initial`/`poll`/`watch` set — confirm no consumer pins the `via` enum).
- Gate the whole block on the actor being a lead (members don't sweep) — read role from the manifest
  once at arm time and capture it, or check inside the sweep helper (the helper already verifies lead).

> Engine-awareness note: this lives in `lib/listener-loop.js`, the engine-agnostic listener subprocess,
> so it applies uniformly to Claude/Copilot/codex leads — no per-harness tool-name branching needed.

### D-003 — turn-boundary hook sweep (backstop + latch-reset home)
Run the SAME `sweepMemberCrashNotifications` helper at the lead's turn boundaries for the
actively-working lead and as the durable home for reset hygiene:
- **`hooks/stop.js`** (lead role): call the sweep **before** the opportunistic `consumeMailbox()` +
  review-required gate. **CORRECTED per F-003:** Stop only drains its own mailbox when
  `listenerState !== 'armed'` (`hooks/stop.js:896`). So the delivery split is: (a) **armed lead**
  (the normal between-turns case) — the sweep appends to the lead's own mailbox and the LISTENER
  delivers it (identical to the D-001 path; the Stop turn itself does NOT surface it, and that is fine);
  (b) **unarmed lead** (listener down/exited) — the sweep appends and Stop's own `consumeMailbox`
  surfaces the crash in the SAME Stop turn. Either way it is delivered. Best-effort try/catch; never
  block the Stop decision on a sweep error. The durable value of the Stop site is the unarmed-backstop
  + being a natural latch-reset home.
- **`hooks/session-start.js`** + **`hooks/pre-tool-use.js`** (lead role): backstop sweeps so an
  actively-working lead notices a crash at the next tool/turn boundary even between heartbeat ticks.
  Cheap because turn boundaries are far less frequent than the 10s heartbeat; the latch dedupes against
  whatever D-001 already delivered.
- All D-003 sites share the same throttle discipline via the latch (the latch IS the idempotency; a
  redundant sweep that finds the signature unchanged appends nothing).

### Envelope-kind wiring (`member-crashed`)
Modeled on `member-left` (system notice) but **review-required AND strict-ack-exempt**:
- `hooks/protocol/envelope.js` — add `'member-crashed'` to `kindEnum`; add a `PAYLOAD_RULES['member-crashed']`
  with required `{ memberName: 'string', deadReason: 'string', signature: 'string', detectedAt: 'string' }`
  (carry `launcherPid`/`launcherStartedAt`/`sessionId` inside `payload` too for forensics, but only the
  stable subset is `required` to keep the validator strict-but-tolerant).
- `hooks/protocol/review-required.js` — add `'member-crashed'` to `DEFAULT_REVIEW_KINDS` (so
  `consumeMailbox` bumps `lastReviewRequiredSeq` and it surfaces in `/crews-review-mail`).
- `hooks/stop.js` — add `'member-crashed'` to `ACK_EXEMPT_KINDS` (so the lead is NOT forced into a
  strict-ack chore for a system notice; the exemption test already requires `from.role==='system'`,
  which `appendSystemMailbox` stamps).

## Scope

### In Scope (v1)
- D-001 throttled heartbeat-tick liveness sweep in the lead listener (CORE) — wakes a quiet idle lead.
- D-003 turn-boundary sweep (Stop primary; SessionStart/PreToolUse backstops) + latch-reset home.
- New `member-crashed` envelope kind: review-required AND strict-ack-exempt, with PAYLOAD_RULES.
- Generation-scoped dedupe latch in `<crewRoot>/liveness-notifications.json`, keyed by lead→member.
- Latch-reset wired into `repairManifestForResume` + clear-member.
- High-confidence-only detection (`state==='dead'`); skip guards for intentional-stop, mid-resume,
  non-member, cross-lead, quiet/unknown.
- **Pre-kill `shutdownRequested:true` intent write in `applyHardStopMember`** (F-001) so an intentional
  hard-stop never false-fires a crash alert during the kill→audit-write window.
- Sweep-before-consume ordering (D-001 self-delivers via the existing `deliver`).
- Standard 6-file version bump + CHANGELOG + AGENTS.md.

### Out of Scope
- **Stalled/idle (9h-dark) detection** — DEFERRED to `crews-member-stalled-needs-attention-nudge`.
  v1 does NOT solve the 9h-dark class (accepted, explicit limitation: those members are `alive`/`quiet`,
  not `dead`).
- **D-002 dying-gasp self-report** — optional fast-path; misses taskkill/T, OS crash, the UNKNOWN/-4094
  lock-bug class. Not v1.
- **Operator escalation / always-on paging** — lead-only in v1; operator escalation is a phase-2 knob.
- Changing `getMemberHealth` detection semantics, `isProcessAlive` EPERM handling, or the listener
  stdout envelope shape.

## Risk Areas
- **False-positive on intentional stop** (HIGH if unguarded) — mitigated by skip guard #2
  (shutdownRequested/terminationKind/terminatedAt) **PLUS the F-001 pre-kill `shutdownRequested:true`
  intent write in `applyHardStopMember`** (without it, the kill→audit-write window at `actors.js:1548→1601`
  false-fires). Dedicated regression test forcing a sweep in that window.
- **False-positive during resume** — mitigated by skip guard #3 (listenerState==='recoverable').
- **Resume re-crash suppressed** (F-002) — mitigated by including `takeoverAt` in the signature
  (resume reliably changes it) PLUS the required explicit latch reset on resume.
- **Latch write-fail after append** (F-006) — accepted fail-loud/fail-duplicate; logged; persist-after-append ordering.
- **Self-deadlock** — the sweep writes the lead's OWN mailbox while the listener consumes it; safe
  because the sweep runs OUTSIDE any mailbox-lock scope (after `markArmed` released its manifest lock),
  the latch uses its OWN lock, and append→deliver→consume is one synchronous unit. No nested locks.
- **Windows lock pressure** — O(members) sync fs + `process.kill` per sweep; mitigated by the ≤1/60s
  throttle (1 in ~6 heartbeat ticks) and EPERM/UNKNOWN-tolerant atomic writes.
- **`via='crash-sweep'`** — verify no consumer pins the listener `via` enum to {initial,poll,watch}.
- **PID-recycle signature collision** — accepted false-negative; defended by `takeoverAt` in the
  signature + explicit reset on resume.
- **Multi-lead cross-notify / orphan miss** — mitigated by guard #5 (`createdByLeadName` ownership +
  `activeLeadNames` single-lead determination) + per-lead latch namespace + `member-crash-sweep-orphan-skipped`
  log for unclaimable null-createdBy members.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A member whose **launcher pid is gone** (`pidAlive===false`) while the lead is **idle on an
  indefinitely-armed listener** results in **exactly one** `member-crashed` `review-required` envelope
  delivered to the lead's mailbox that **wakes the armed listener**, within the sweep cadence (≤ ~60s) —
  verified by a synthetic dead-member fixture + an armed lead listener asserting a single delivery.
- For the **no-launcher-pid + stale-heartbeat** dead case, the notification arrives within
  `HEARTBEAT_STALE_MS` (5min) + the sweep cadence (≤ ~60s) — NOT within the cadence alone (F-007 honest
  latency split; `deriveHealthState` does not classify this case `dead` until heartbeat age ≥
  `HEARTBEAT_STALE_MS`, `hooks/health.js:54-57`).
- A `quiet`, `unknown`, healthy-`alive`, intentionally-stopped, or mid-resume (`recoverable`) member
  produces **zero** `member-crashed` envelopes. This includes a member observed during the
  `applyHardStopMember` kill→audit-write window: with the F-001 pre-kill `shutdownRequested:true` intent
  write, a sweep forced into that window sees the intent marker and skips (regression test required).
- Repeated sweeps over the same already-dead incarnation produce **no duplicate** notifications
  (generation-latch idempotency).
- After `/resume-crew` of a crashed member, a subsequent re-crash of the new incarnation produces a
  **fresh** notification (new signature; latch reset verified); `/clear-member` clears the latch entry.
- `member-crashed` is review-required (surfaces in `/crews-review-mail`, bumps `lastReviewRequiredSeq`)
  but does NOT force a strict-ack (modeled on `member-left`).
- D-003 turn-boundary sweep: for an **armed** lead, a freshly-detected crash is appended to the lead's
  own mailbox and delivered by the listener (the Stop turn itself does not surface it — `stop.js:896`);
  for an **unarmed** lead, the crash surfaces in the SAME Stop turn via Stop's own `consumeMailbox`.
  Idempotent across turns via the same latch.
- crews suite green via `node tests/run.js`; `node --check` clean on touched files; version bumped via
  `scripts/bump-version.js 3.13.0`; `manifestFields.length===51` test UNCHANGED (no new manifest field).

## Preliminary Story Decomposition
- US-001 — `member-crashed` envelope-kind wiring (kindEnum, PAYLOAD_RULES, DEFAULT_REVIEW_KINDS,
  ACK_EXEMPT_KINDS) + envelope-kind test.
- US-002 — `getMemberHealth` STRICTLY-ADDITIVE return fields (sessionId, createdBy, role, takeoverAt,
  shutdownRequested, terminationKind, terminatedAt) + health.test assertion (new fields present,
  existing shape + snapshotCrew/list-members behavior unchanged).
- US-003 — `hooks/member-crash-notifications.js` helper (signature incl. takeoverAt, locked atomic
  latch with persist-after-append, sweep with all 6 skip guards using `createdByLeadName` +
  `activeLeadNames`, orphan-skip log, reset) + the F-001 pre-kill `shutdownRequested:true` intent write
  in `hooks/actors.js::applyHardStopMember` + unit tests (each guard, single-delivery, dedupe,
  intentional-stop-during-kill-window, latch-write-fail).
- US-004 — D-001: throttled sweep in the listener heartbeat tick + self-deliver + integration test.
- US-005 — D-003: lead Stop/SessionStart/PreToolUse backstop sweeps + latch-reset into
  repairManifestForResume + clear-member + reset test.
- US-006 — Version bump (6 files + version.test.js) + CHANGELOG + AGENTS.md `## v3.13.0`.

## Suggested Decomposition
Single serial cluster. Every story is in `plugins/crews/` and the stories share load-bearing files
(`hooks/protocol/envelope.js`, `hooks/stop.js`, `hooks/member-crash-notifications.js`,
`lib/listener-loop.js`) plus strict ordering (envelope kind must exist before the sweep appends it; the
helper must exist before D-001/D-003 call it; the version bump must be last). There is no
parallelizable disjoint surface — do NOT split into parallel clusters.

### Cluster: member-crash-autonotify
- Stories: US-001, US-002, US-003, US-004, US-005, US-006
- Phase: 1
- Depends on: None
- File-overlap evidence: shared=[`hooks/protocol/envelope.js`, `hooks/stop.js`, `hooks/health.js`,
  `lib/listener-loop.js`, `hooks/member-crash-notifications.js`, version files]; exclusive=[]; risk=high
- `execution_mode` rationale: All stories mutate a small shared set of crews files with hard ordering
  dependencies (kind → helper → hooks → version bump). Serial execution in one impl member is correct;
  parallel clusters would conflict on envelope.js/stop.js and the 6 version stamps.

Parallel handoff: `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan <plan_job_dir>/plan.md --parallel --suggested-decomposition <plan_job_dir>/suggested-decomposition.json`
(Not recommended here — single serial cluster.)

## Open Questions
- **Latch home** — RESOLVED in plan: `<crewRoot>/liveness-notifications.json` keyed `lead→member→signature`
  (separate file, not member manifest / not `manifest.custom`). Avoids the `manifestFields.length===51`
  churn AND the `repairManifestForResume` write-race; multi-lead clean.
- **`getMemberHealth` extension vs sweep-reads-manifest** — RESOLVED: extend `getMemberHealth` return
  (additive, single-source). Impl may instead read the manifest in the sweep if extending the shared
  health API proves to touch too many callers — either satisfies the ACs.
- **D-001 self-deliver vs rely on fs.watch** — RESOLVED: explicit `deliver('crash-sweep')` after append
  for immediacy. (fs.watch self-notification + the ≤1s poll backstop would also work but adds latency;
  the explicit call is the append-before-consume guarantee the spawn-prompt requires.)
- Should the `member-crashed` payload carry the full `health` object or only the stable signature subset?
  Plan recommends the stable subset as `required` in PAYLOAD_RULES + the rest under `payload` for
  forensics; the impl reviewer should confirm strict-schema tolerance.

## Plan Review Findings (Phase 4 convergence — all resolved into the plan above)

Multi-model review ran Claude (no issues — shallow), Copilot lens (3 High + 4 Medium), and a
rubber-duck design critique (2 High + 2 Medium). Codex review lens timed out (exit 124 — the known
Windows codex-exec hang; non-blocking). All High/Medium findings were verified against source and folded
into the Approach / Skip-guards / ACs / Risks / Stories above (manual convergence; the codex-engine
review-loop was bypassed because the codex lens hangs on this box):

| ID | Sev | Source | Finding | Resolution |
|----|-----|--------|---------|------------|
| F-001 | High | rubber-duck | `applyHardStopMember` kills BEFORE writing shutdown markers (`actors.js:1548→1601`); guard #2 alone false-fires in that window | Hoist a pre-kill `shutdownRequested:true` intent write into `applyHardStopMember`; in-scope; regression test forcing a sweep in the window |
| F-002 | High | rubber-duck | Resume reset is load-bearing, NOT hygiene: same-session resume reuses `sessionId` and `launcher.pid` lags (`actors.js:2435`), so a re-crash keeps the old signature | Add `takeoverAt` (`actors.js:522,533`) to the signature; reframe reset as REQUIRED |
| F-003 | High | copilot | D-003 Stop only consumes when `listenerState!=='armed'` (`stop.js:896`); an armed lead's Stop won't surface the crash same-turn | Reframed D-003: armed→listener delivers; unarmed→Stop consume surfaces; ACs split |
| F-004 | High | rubber-duck + copilot (consensus) | Null-`createdBy` members exist (`assignMemberRole` `actors.js:719`); raw `createdBy.leadName` + raw `readCrewMeta().leads` miss them / mis-claim across tombstoned leads | Use `createdByLeadName()` + `activeLeadNames()`; log `member-crash-sweep-orphan-skipped` |
| F-005 | Med | copilot | `snapshotCrew` calls `getMemberHealth` for ALL actors; a non-additive change regresses list-members | Extension is STRICTLY additive; health.test asserts unchanged shape |
| F-006 | Med | copilot | Latch write-fail after a successful append could duplicate | Persist-after-append; fail-loud/fail-duplicate + `member-crash-latch-write-failed` log; unit test |
| F-007 | Med | rubber-duck + copilot (consensus) | AC "within sweep cadence" overpromises for the no-pid case (needs `HEARTBEAT_STALE_MS` first) | ACs split: pid-gone ≤ ~60s; no-pid ≤ `HEARTBEAT_STALE_MS` + cadence |

**Verified sound (no change needed):** `deliver` is a hoisted declaration callable from the heartbeat
callback (`listener-loop.js:356`); `deliver` exits via `markExited`+`finish({type:'messages'})`; the
v3.6.2 epoch fence passes for the lead's own current listener (`mailbox.js:670-687`); no
double-delivery race (the `resolved` guard + JS non-interleaving within a tick).
